people.name: Lily Vadera
people.bio: Mrs. Lily Vadera, has over 34 years of experience in Central banking. She is a M.A in International Relations. She retired as an Executive Director from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in October 2020. As the Executive Director of the RBI, she was in-charge of the Department of Regulation (DoR) where she dealt with the regulatory framework for various entities in financial sector, covering all categories of banks and non-banking finance companies. During her tenure in RBI, Mrs. Vadera represented the RBI in various international forums such as the Policy Development Group of Basel Committee on Banking Supervision of BIS, Switzerland, Financial Stability Board and the Sub-groups of the G-20 on SME financing and Green financing. Mrs. Vadera also represented RBI on a committee set up by the Government on SME financing. Mrs. Vadera was instrumental in putting in place a framework for a regulatory sandbox to provide an enabling environment for fintech players to foster innovation in financial services and played a significant role in the amalgamation of banks in stress. She represented RBI and played an important role as a member of the Insolvency Law Committee set up by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA).

The total aggregation of the issue amounts to Rs. 57,99,99,97,400. These warrants are convertible into equivalent equity shares with a face value of Rs. 1 each. This disclosure is made under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015. The company has informed the BSE and NSE regarding this corporate action.

The warrants are convertible into equity shares pari passu with existing fully paid-up shares. Upon issuance, a minimum of 25 percent of the consideration is payable on the date of allotment. The remaining 75 percent is payable when the options against the warrants are exercised. Operating profit was 134.3 billion yen, a decrease of 0.6 percent. Profit before tax stood at 156.5 billion yen, down 24.5 percent. Foreign exchange rates and raw material prices were cited as external factors affecting results. Capital expenditures were 87.3 billion yen. Interest-bearing debt balance was 736.0 billion yen. Cash balance was 930.0 billion yen. The filing was submitted by Sanjeev Grover, Executive Officer and Company Secretary.
